question.leadin: This man was the first president of Gran Colombia, and he won the battles of Boyaca and Carabobo.
question.text: Name this South American leader known as "The Liberator."
question.answerHtml: Simón Bolívar [or Simón José Antonio de la Santísima Trinidad Bolívar Palacios Ponte y Blanco]
question.clue: In 1822, he met Jose de San Martin at the Guayaquil Conference.

swap.text: This man headed Haiti from 1971 to 1986 and returned in January 2011. He was quickly arrested and charged with corruption.
swap.clue: This Haitian dictator whose extravagant 1980 marriage to Michele Bennett Parquet led to popular discontent that culminated in his 1986 exile. He succeeded his father of the same name in 1971.

question.leadin: Former secretary of state John Kerry claimed that this country was a "narco-kleptocracy."
question.text: Name this Central American country once led by Manuel Noriega that separated from Colombia in 1903. It was invaded by the United States in Operation Just Cause in 1989.
question.clue: Operation Nifty Package sunk the boat of a leader of this country, who subsequently hid in its Vatican diplomatic mission.

swap.leadin: In 1948, the assassination of Jorge Eli´ecer Gait´an set off riots and started a decade-long civil war.
swap.text: Name this South American country where the ensuing riots ravaged the capital city and earned the name El Bogotazo [bo-gah-TAH-zo].
swap.clue: Earlier this country had fought Spain for its independence at the Battle of Boyaca.

question.leadin: This man took power after La Moneda was attacked in 1973.
question.text: Identify this South American military dictator who succeeded Salvador Allende. The 1991 Rettig Commision asserted that over 2000 political prisoners were executed under his tenure.
question.clue: On his 60th birthday, the CIA launched Operation Condor to suppress left-wing movements in this man's nation and neighboring Argentina.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about international relations in the Caribbean.
swap.text: The US invaded this island nation in 1983 in which US intelligence agencies lied about mass graves caused by communist brutality to drum up support. Cuba sent aid for this nation, such as teachers, to its capital of St. George's.
swap.clue: This country's first prime minister was Eric Gairy, whose overthrow led to concerns over the length of Point Salines International Airport and the safety of students at St. George's University.

question.text: Following the war, the U.S. also acquired this territory, which was granted limited self-governance by the Foraker Act. Separatists from this place tried to assassinate Harry Truman in 1950.
question.clue: Troops led by Nelson Miles took possession of this island in 1898.

swap.leadin: During this time period, Bernardo Reyes was killed in a key battle shortly after being freed from prison.
swap.text: Identify this short period in 1913 during which the nephew of a former president conspired to bring down the presidency of a certain country.
swap.clue: This 1913 coup nominally led by Aureliano Blanquet against the Mexican government under Madero, which received substantial support from American ambassador Henry Lane Wilson.

question.text: Haiti's national anthem is named in honor of this man, who became the first ruler of an independent Haiti after the uprising led by Toussaint L'Ouverture. He was overthrown by a group including Alexandre Petion.
question.clue: Along with Francois Capois, he had led the troops that overwhelmed the soldiers of Donatien de Rochambeau at the Battle of Vertiere, which ended Napoleon's invasion of his country.

swap.text: The first native peoples encountered by Christopher Columbus were the Taino, a subgroup of this group of Indians, who were wiped out in Hispaniola by diseases brought in the encounter.
swap.clue: This tribe was the first Native American people to meet with Christopher Columbus upon his landing at Hispanola.

question.text: , Plutarco Calles, 1934. Under his six-year term, private land was distributed to peasants and all foreign-owned oil properties were nationalized.
question.clue: This politician cited Article 27 of his country's constitution in violating an agreement his predecessor made with Dwight Morrow.

swap.leadin: This man lost a controversial 1990 election to Fernando Collor de Melo and this leader of the Workers' Party was eventually elected president on his fourth attempt.
swap.text: Name this former world leader who was succeeded by Dilma Rousseff in 2011. In 2018, he was arrested on corruption charges and later dropped out of his country's October presidential elections.
swap.clue: This man finished second in the first-round election but lost to Collor in the runoff. He lost in the 1994 and 1998 presidential elections before finally winning, on his fourth attempt, in 2002.

question.text: The Lei Aurea was issued by this last emperor of Brazil, the husband of Teresa Cristina, who was overthrown by Deodora de Fonseca.
question.clue: This man's nation defeated the forces of Juan Manuel de Rosas in the Platine War, during which his army was led by the Duke of Caxias.

swap.leadin: The Huilliche and these people razed settlements south of the Biobio River during the Destruction of the Seven Cities, which caused settlers to concentrate in the Central Valley instead.
swap.text: Name these indigenous people who maintained their independence through long wars with the Spanish and adopted the horse to carry out Malon raids.
swap.clue: Conquistador Pedro de Valdivia's prolonged 16th century campaign to conquer these people during the Arauco ] War ended in his death.

question.text: Jamaican workers had originally arrived to work on the Panama Railway, constructed after the U.S. signed the Mallarino-Bidlack Treaty with this short-lived country. Francisco Santander led this successor state to Gran Colombia, which shares its name with the viceroyalty whose territory it comprised
question.answerHtml: Republic of New Granada [or República de la Nueva Granada]

swap.leadin: One politician of this name resigned after his country succeeded from the West Indies Federation in a referendum, leading to the federation's dissolution.
swap.text: Give this surname shared by Caribbean politicians Norman and Michael, a father and son who both led the People's National Party.
swap.clue: A leader with this surname was pressured by the U.S. to expel the "4 H's" from his party over suspicions of communism.

question.text: Before returning to power in 2007, Ortega was unseated in the 1990 election by a politician and former ally of this surname. The murder of a La Prensa editor with this surname was a major spark of the Sandinista revolution.
question.clue: Pedro Joaquin of this family was an ardent anti-Somoza partisan who was assassinated in the early '80s. Pedro's wife Violeta defeated Daniel Ortega to became the President of Nicaragua in 1990.

swap.text: After deposition of Machado, Fulgencio Batista ruled Cuba until overthrown by this man in the 26th of July Movement. He ended a 1953 speech by declaring "History Will Absolve Me."
swap.clue: Many emigrants left this ruler's country when he opened up the port of Mariel.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Argentina's economic woes since the 1970s.
question.text: This was Argentina's currency at the time of Menem's election. Juan Vital Sourrouille ("soo-REEL") introduced this currency in 1985 under a namesake economic plan, but it only lasted until 1991 before being replaced by the convertible peso.

swap.text: In 1825, this Argentine backed group led by Juan Lavalleja had steadily gained the support of ruler Uruguayans to throw out the Portuguese and dismantle the Cisplatine Republic.
swap.answerHtml: Thirty Three Immortals [or Band of 33; or Los treinta y tres; accept equivalents]
